report.summary: Chunk 6 of correctness.py: validates task dict fields, defines is_correctness_task, disposable_worktree, apply_test_overlay, reference_patch.
risks: line 670 | high | apply_test_overlay writes files from git show verbatim; if test_revision is user-controlled, arbitrary content could be written to worktree. | Confirm that test_revision is validated or comes from trusted source.

line 673 | medium | _git_read and _safe_join are imported but not defined in this chunk; if they are missing or behave unexpectedly, the function will fail. | Check that these symbols exist in the module or are imported correctly.

handoff.purpose: Validates task dict, defines is_correctness_task, disposable_worktree, apply_test_overlay, and starts reference_patch.

symbols.name: validate_correctness_task
symbols.note: Validates a task dict for correctness format; returns list of problem strings.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Returns True if task dict matches correctness format; delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task.

symbols.name: disposable_worktree
symbols.note: Context manager that creates a temporary git worktree at a given revision, yields its path, and cleans up.

symbols.name: apply_test_overlay
symbols.note: Writes files from a given revision into the worktree verbatim (test overlay).

symbols.name: reference_patch
symbols.note: Returns git diff between base and reference revisions, excluding specified paths.

claims.text: cannot fail is the exact defect ``harness._recall``'s vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: Refers to harness._recall and a repo defect; no such code in this chunk.

claims.text: True for a task carrying the correctness format. Mirrored in ``daedalus.eval.tasks`` so the harness can refuse to grade one with substring recall; defined there, re-exported here for callers who already have this module imported.
claims.why: The function does import from daedalus.eval.tasks and delegates; the comment describes exactly this behavior.

claims.text: A checkout of ``revision`` that is NOT the primary checkout.
claims.why: The function creates a worktree using GitWorktreeManager, which places it outside the primary checkout.

claims.text: Delegates to :class:`daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager` on purpose rather than shelling out to ``git worktree add``: that class places worktrees outside the checkout, refuses an allocation whose path is repo-adjacent, and owns a recursive delete that re-verifies every component before every syscall.
claims.why: The code uses GitWorktreeManager and its create_worktree/cleanup_worktree methods; the docstring describes its intended behavior.

claims.text: Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no ``shutil.rmtree`` here and there must never be one.
claims.why: The cleanup uses manager.cleanup_worktree and manager.reap_branches; no shutil.rmtree appears in this chunk.

claims.text: The branch ref that ``git worktree add -b`` writes into the shared ``.git`` is reaped afterwards through the manager's own ``reap_branches``, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.
claims.why: The finally block calls manager.reap_branches(), and the docstring describes its policy.

claims.text: This is SWE-bench's "test patch", and it is what makes a before-state measurable at all: the base revision predates the fix, so it also predates the fix's tests -- running a FAIL_TO_PASS node against a bare base checkout would only ever report ``missing``.
claims.why: Refers to SWE-bench and FAIL_TO_PASS behavior; no such context in this chunk.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (``git show <rev>:<path>``), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
claims.why: The code uses _git_read which captures stdout bytes and writes them via target.write_bytes; no decoding occurs.

claims.text: Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` if a path does not exist at that revision, and :class:`OverlayEscape` if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: The code raises FileNotFoundError when git show fails; OverlayEscape is presumably raised by _safe_join (not shown but referenced).

claims.text: The known-good change as a patch: ``git diff base..reference``.
claims.why: The function constructs a git diff command with those arguments.

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the "after" run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: The function accepts an exclude parameter and passes it to git diff via '--' and the excluded paths; the docstring explains the reasoning.

observations.what: validate_correctness_task validates task dict fields and returns list of problems; no side effects.
is_correctness_task delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task, avoiding duplication.
disposable_worktree uses GitWorktreeManager for worktree creation and cleanup, with branch reaping.
apply_test_overlay writes files verbatim from git show; raises FileNotFoundError for missing paths.
reference_patch starts definition but is incomplete; it constructs git diff command with --binary, --no-color, etc.
The chunk imports _git_read, _safe_join, _refuse_primary_checkout, GitWorktreeManager, and uuid; these are assumed defined elsewhere.
